title: Dock a Nintendo Switch: lower the console straight down its dock's slot until its port seats on the hidden USB-C plug
instruction: Put the console in its dock so it connects.
context: Most people with a Nintendo Switch put it back in its dock to play on the TV or to charge it: the console goes straight down the dock's slot until the USB-C plug at the bottom, out of sight, enters the port on the console's lower edge. The slot is only about a millimetre wider than the console on each side and the plug is a sliver 8.25 by 2.4 millimetres, so the console has to come down upright and centred, then take a firm push over the last few millimetres. Tilted or off to one side, its port lands beside the plug and the console rests in the dock unconnected: nothing shows on the TV and it does not charge. Dropped in from a height, it can bend a real plug. Here a Switch OLED with both Joy-Con attached lies screen down on a rest in front of its dock. Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo, named for identification only.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A Nintendo Switch dock with LAN port (Nintendo: about 4.1 x 6.9 x 2.0 in; here 104 x 175 x 51 mm, 313 g) stands on the bench centred at (30, -10), its 175 mm length along y. Its slot, 16 mm wide (x) and 45 mm deep, runs the whole length along y; at the middle of the slot's floor stands a USB-C plug, 8.25 x 2.4 mm (USB Type-C plug size), 6.5 mm tall, with a chamfered tip. A fixed rest, 120 mm high, 66 x 140 mm, stands centred at (47, -10). A Nintendo Switch OLED model with both Joy-Con attached (Nintendo: 102 x 242 x 13.9 mm; 420 g) lies on it screen down, centred at (46, -10), its 242 mm width along y and its port, a pocket 9.25 x 3.4 mm and 6.6 mm deep in the middle of its lower edge, toward the robot's far side (+x). Its top edge overhangs the rest by 30 mm toward the robot, so one jaw can close on the edge's 13.9 mm thickness. Seated, the console stands upright in the slot, screen toward the robot, its port fully on the plug; reaching that takes 8 N beyond the console's weight over the last 6 mm. Slot width and depth, plug height, port pocket, the 8 N and the frictions (dock and console on bench and in the slot 0.4) are estimates: Nintendo publishes no slot or plug figures. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. For a real trial: the dock's AC adapter plugged in, an HDMI cable to a display, and the console awake; or watch the dock's LED.
scoring: Judged once both grippers are at least 3 cm from the console and everything has been still for 1 s. 1.0: the port fully on the plug (the plug in to within 0.7 mm of its stop; real trial: the TV shows the console's picture), the console upright within 2 degrees with its screen toward the robot, arrived at the plug slower than 0.25 m/s, and the dock within 2 cm and 5 degrees of where it stood. 0.5: the console resting upright (within 5 degrees) in the slot with its port not on the plug, or dropped in faster than 0.25 m/s, dock kept. 0.25: its lower edge inside the slot's mouth but jammed tilted. 0: not in the slot, or the dock moved or tipped. Real trial: 1.0 is the TV picture or a lit LED (AC adapter, HDMI cable, display, console awake), the console upright by eye, the dock not moved; the speed and tilt limits are simulator checks. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz), about 2.4 times the 25 s scripted demo
reset_notes: The console screen down on its rest, top edge toward the robot; the dock at its mark. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies on GPU. Console 102 x 242 x 13.9 mm, 420 g, and dock 104 x 175 x 51 mm, 313 g, are boxes at Nintendo's sizes (no public CAD found); the Joy-Con are not separate parts. Slot width and depth, plug height, port pocket, frictions and the 8 N seat are estimates. The 8 N is code: a pull out of the port over the plug's last 6 mm of travel. Video and charging are not simulated: the scorer reads the port on the plug. The demo reads the console's pose.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in its 1,200 steps; demo: 1.0
